key_insight: Trainable quantum channels can be used as non-unitary, learnable building blocks that expand quantum models beyond unitary-only dynamics and improve learning optimization.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical framework for designing quantum learning architectures that exploit open-system effects, potentially yielding better performance than standard variational circuits.
method: Reformulate quantum channels as trainable computational primitives in a quantum learning model.
Use Kraus-operator-based channel dynamics to create multiple functional components and adaptive effective observables.
Generalize conventional unitary models by including non-unitary degrees of freedom and richer optimization directions.
evidence_signal: Experiments on classification tasks with trainable amplitude-damping and phase-damping channels showed improved optimization behavior and predictive performance.
watch_item: Training and hardware implementation may be sensitive to noise modeling, channel parameterization, and the difficulty of accurately realizing controllable non-unitary operations.
paper_title: Trainable Quantum Channels as Computational Primitives for Quantum Learning
